simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to פִּגּוּל (H6292) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: פִּגּוּל (piggûwl) means properly, fetid , i.e. (figuratively) unclean (ceremonially) First listed occurrence: Ezek 4 14.

definitions.full: H6292. piggul [ מִּגּוּל ] noun masculine Lev 7:18 foul thing, refuse , but only as technical term of unclean sacrificial flesh; — it is ׳פ if eaten on third day 7:18 (P), 19:7 (H); compare פ ׳בְּשַׂר Ezek 4:14 (undefined); plural מִּגֻּלִים מְרַק Isa 65:4 broth of refuse things (Kt פרק ), RS Sem i. 325, 2nd ed. 343 thinks of flesh with the blood; Du on the passage of mice and other unclean animals .
definitions.rootNote: or פִּגֻּל ; from an unused root meaning to stink ;
